strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing genuine limitations in existing GUI benchmarks: reproducibility, ambiguous evaluation, insufficient long-horizon task assessment, and single-path bias
Innovative Causal Pathway design providing deterministic failure signals via 'Path Collapse' with programmatic verification and unambiguous error attribution
Comprehensive multi-level evaluation framework (WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR, error attribution) enabling both holistic and fine-grained performance assessment
High-quality rigorously curated dataset with 523 human-verified trajectories, enforced grounding, preserved behavioral diversity, and detailed reasoning traces suitable for process supervision
Solid experimental methodology with diverse model evaluations, clear architectural ablation showing LightManus advantage, generalization testing on A3 benchmark, and interpretable error analysis
Practical insights revealing model capability ceilings, limited generalization of fine-tuning to complex tasks, and bottleneck identification (OE vs KD vs PE) across different model scales
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: LightManus is primarily straightforward hierarchical composition of existing agents (PC-Agent, Mobile-Agent-e) lacking fundamental innovation or component-level ablations

Benchmark design inherently limited to structured sequential tasks: Causal Pathways enforce strict linear dependencies that may not reflect real-world workflow flexibility or alternative valid solution paths

Insufficient scale and diversity analysis: Only 276 tasks and 523 trajectories (278 for training) by modern standards; missing breakdown of task types, application distribution, inter-task dependencies, and potential data contamination risks

Weak fine-tuning results undermining RFT contributions: Improvement from 3.3% to 10.8% WPSR on Qwen2.5-VL-7B is modest, lacks comparison with supervised fine-tuning and alternative strategies, and shows fundamental capacity limits not addressable by fine-tuning
Critical missing inter-rater agreement statistics and lack of ablation studies on curation principles (e.g., impact of 'grounded execution' enforcement), limiting interpretability of results
Unvalidated weighting schemes: WPSR difficulty weighting (proportional to nodes/applications) and p-ATSR positional weighting lack human validation or sensitivity analysis

Limited theoretical contribution with expected findings: Results that model scale matters and fine-tuning has limited generalization are unsurprising; insufficient guidance on building better agents beyond documenting limitations

Incomplete analysis: No systematic investigation of task type hardness, missing detailed comparison with other recent benchmarks (WebArena, GAIA), no cost-benefit analysis vs existing benchmarks, limited exploration of 'over-planning' phenomenon

strengths: Clear problem motivation: identifies genuine limitations in GUI agent benchmarks (ambiguous verification, reproducibility, multiple solution paths)
Well-structured benchmark design: Causal Pathways with atomic tasks and deterministic Path Collapse provide clear evaluation framework
Comprehensive multi-level evaluation framework: WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR, and error attribution analysis provide multiple perspectives
Careful dataset curation: 523 human-verified trajectories with preservation of diverse behaviors and self-corrections
Thorough model evaluation: tests diverse foundation models (proprietary and open-source) with consistent metrics
Detailed error analysis: categorization into KD/PE/OE provides diagnostic insights into failure modes
weaknesses: Fundamental scope mismatch: This is a GUI automation paper, not NLP research; lacks relevance to computational linguistics and poorly suited for ACL venues

Limited technical novelty: Causal Pathways is straightforward task decomposition; LightManus is hierarchical scheduling without architectural innovation; T-RFT lacks clear distinction from standard SFT

Missing critical ablations: No ablation studies on LightManus components; LightManus-Flash (31.1% p-ATSR) vs. MAe-Pro (31.6% p-ATSR) shows negligible difference, insufficient to support architectural claims

Weak fine-tuning evaluation: Only one small model fine-tuned; T-RFT improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B WPSR 3.3%→10.8% but fails to generalize (drops to 4.7% on Level-3 tasks); no comparison to SFT or alternative methods; no statistical significance testing

Key methodological details undefined or missing: exact WPSR difficulty formula unclear; p-ATSR positional weight function p(i) never specified (critical for reproducibility); no inter-annotator agreement for manual error classification

Acknowledged benchmark limitations unaddressed: authors admit NaturalGAIA 'does not fully capture the dynamic nature of real-world interfaces'—static evaluation is fundamental design constraint; only 276 tasks with limited diversity

Overclaiming: marginal improvements presented as substantial; T-RFT gains don't generalize despite framed as learning generalizable principles; claims of formidable challenge unclear on fixed benchmark
Reproducibility concerns: relies on proprietary models; human verification process non-deterministic; many details relegated to appendices; data/code not provided with submission
Incomplete experimental design: no error bars or confidence intervals; inconsistent evaluation protocols (Pass@1 vs Pass@4); limited generalization study (only 6 A3 subsets)
Presentation overload: attempts three separate contributions (benchmark, agent architecture, fine-tuning) without justifying integration; dense results tables; key details missing from main text

strengths: Well-motivated benchmark design: Causal Pathways principle effectively balances reproducibility with realism, addressing real limitations in existing GUI agent benchmarks through deterministic task structure and programmatic verification
Comprehensive multi-level evaluation framework: WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR, and detailed error attribution (KD/PE/OE) enable both macroscopic and microscopic analysis with clear theoretical justification

High-quality, carefully curated dataset: Two-phase collection (LLM + expert verification) with principled curation criteria (grounded execution enforcement, preservation of behavioral diversity and self-correction) demonstrates methodological rigor

Thorough experimental evaluation: Diverse foundation models tested with insightful findings about model scaling effects, architectural benefits of LightManus (40% improvement over baselines in Pass@1 SR), and differential error patterns across model sizes

Strong empirical results validating benchmark difficulty: Even state-of-the-art Claude-sonnet-4 achieves only 34.6% WPSR on complex tasks, demonstrating genuine challenge; error analysis reveals distinct bottlenecks (Operational Errors for large models, Structural Compliance for smaller models)
Generalization evidence: 40% relative improvement on A3 benchmark with unseen applications suggests T-RFT learns generalizable principles rather than task memorization
Clear presentation and community value: Well-written paper with effective figures and actionable insights; public dataset release will provide ongoing research value
weaknesses: Limited novelty in LightManus architecture: Hierarchical decomposition (parsing → scheduling → execution) is standard practice; stages leverage existing agents (Mobile-Agent-e, PC-Agent) without substantial innovation; architectural advantages not sufficiently decomposed via ablation studies

T-RFT evaluation lacks rigor and baselines: No SFT baseline comparison to substantiate claims about superiority; results underwhelming (3.3%→10.8% WPSR with sharp degradation to 4.7% at Level-3); no comparison with other fine-tuning approaches; sensitivity to data quantity/quality unexplored

Dataset quality assurance concerns: Only 2 annotators for curation raises bias/consistency risks; no inter-annotator agreement reported; no quantification of self-corrective trajectories; sparse coverage (~1.9 trajectories per task)

Incomplete experimental reporting: Missing Pass@4 results for GPT-o3 and Claude-sonnet-4 unexplained; training details in appendix limiting reproducibility; no ablations on LightManus components; no statistical significance testing

Benchmark scope limitations: 276 tasks is moderate with no task diversity analysis; acknowledged limitation that benchmark doesn't capture dynamic real-world interfaces; task difficulty stratification (length + applications) lacks empirical validation

Limited comparative analysis: Single generalization test (A3 benchmark, Qwen only); no GAIA benchmark comparison despite conceptual relevance; missing ablations on why T-RFT fails on complex tasks; error analysis lacks guidance for addressing specific failure modes

Reproducibility concerns: LLM behavior varies with version/configuration; data contamination risk not addressed; code availability and release timeline not mentioned; difficulty reproducing MLLM results

Presentation issues: WPSR difficulty weighting scheme (nodes + applications) lacks justification; some redundancy between abstract and introduction; 'Causal Pathways' terminology slightly oversells concept (is essentially atomic task sequences with dependency checking)

strengths: Well-motivated problem articulation addressing the 'Evaluation-Realism Dilemma' with clear examples of tensions between realistic and verifiable benchmarks

Systematic benchmark construction methodology using Wikidata, with principled three-stage pipeline (path generation, tool grounding, narrative injection) that decouples logical structure from linguistic presentation
Comprehensive multi-level evaluation framework (WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR) enabling fine-grained error attribution beyond binary success rates, with detailed error categorization and examples
Extensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Gemini, Claude, Qwen, GPT-5.2), detailed ablations isolating macro/micro components, and cross-benchmark validation (AndroidWorld, Mind2Web)
Significant practical efficiency improvements: 74% token reduction and 75% execution time reduction, validated through efficiency analysis
Thorough documentation with rigorous design principles (Appendix A), complete task creation pipeline details, and full execution trajectory examples supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Severely limited dataset scope: only 276 tasks with restrictive constraints excluding dynamic/irreversible scenarios (e-commerce, messaging, real-time data), making results potentially unrepresentative of real GUI interaction; freeze-frame strategy for time-sensitive data is artificial

Manual verification bottleneck explicitly acknowledged ('scalability is bottlenecked by manual verification') with no inter-annotator agreement metrics, annotation guidelines, or cost analysis provided, undermining scalability claims

Limited framework novelty: macro-planning + micro-execution paradigm and hybrid perception are acknowledged as existing approaches; Context Evolution (Eq. 5) is vaguely described as simple parameter substitution; primary contribution is engineering rather than methodological innovation

Experimental fairness issues: comparing Claude-Sonnet-4.5 (45.6%) against Gemini-2.5-Pro Mobile-Agent-e (21.1%) uses different models, conflating architectural gains with model scale; Pass@4 metrics incomplete for several models; absolute performance remains modest

Critical metric definition omissions: p-ATSR weighting function p(i) defined only as 'monotonically increasing' without specification (linear? exponential?), making reproducibility impossible; WPSR difficulty weighting rationale unjustified; error attribution is manual without inter-rater reliability

Generalization concerns: AndroidWorld validation (63.3%) exceeds NaturalGAIA results (45.6%), suggesting possible overfitting; Mind2Web comparison limited to web-only subset with different evaluation criteria; no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals provided

Severe technical clarity gaps: Equation 8 relationship between reasoning and action encoding is unclear; Context Evolution implementation details missing; MATCR only counts consecutive successes from start; Task Topology parsing constraints not specified

Scope limitations reduce applicability: benchmark constrained to 25 applications with immutable historical records, unrepresentative of typical mobile ecosystems; acknowledged unresolved issues (inference latency, cumulative error propagation, state drift) persist without proposed solutions

strengths: Addresses a real problem: the evaluation-realism dilemma in GUI agent benchmarking is well-motivated and clearly articulated
Comprehensive technical documentation with detailed design principles and extensive appendices providing implementation details and examples
Multi-level evaluation framework (WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR) offers more granular assessment than typical single-metric evaluation, with error attribution providing interpretability
Systematic experimental evaluation across 7-10 foundation models with consistent evaluation protocols and demonstrated efficiency gains (75% token reduction, 76% time improvement)
Honest acknowledgment of limitations: authors transparently discuss constraints around manual verification, temporal dynamics, and determinism requirements
weaknesses: Fundamental problem-solution mismatch: paper claims to address evaluation-realism dilemma but then exacerbates it by creating a maximally constrained benchmark that excludes dynamic scenarios, irreversible operations, and temporal dynamics, sacrificing ecological validity for verifiability

Severely limited benchmark scope: only 276 tasks (vs. Mind2Web's 2,350), 25 applications, three-level task difficulty stratification is coarse (1-2 to 5-7 nodes), and frequent Pass@4 inflation (60-100%) suggests insufficient task complexity

Weak novelty: modular planning-execution architecture, hybrid perception, and knowledge-graph-based task generation are not novel; paper primarily combines existing techniques without significant conceptual advance

Incomplete ablation studies: only one partial ablation (LightManus-MAe vs. LightManus-Jarvis with different baselines), missing ablations for context evolution module, error categories, and component trade-offs

Methodological concerns: manual verification bottleneck (not scalable), freeze-frame strategy unrealistic for many queries, determinism assumption ignores LLM stochasticity, state validation via screenshots+XML may miss logical validity issues

Unfair baseline comparisons: different observation spaces (Table 1) confound architecture effects with perception modality; low absolute performance (45.6% best case) raises questions about benchmark design vs. agent capability

Missing technical clarity: context evolution module E_φ (Eq. 5) lacks algorithmic description, task parser P_θ lacks constraint/generation details, consistency check V(r_t) undefined, no example walkthrough of key mechanisms
Weak generalization evidence: AndroidWorld results on single model only, Mind2Web comparison restricted to web subset, no analysis of which design elements transfer to other domains
Reproducibility failures: code link missing (shows empty period), dataset versioning for Wikidata unclear, LLM prompts for context evolution/parsing not provided, hyperparameter details sparse

Questionable 'naturalness' claims: sequence shuffling and noise injection do not capture realistic cognitive non-linearity; real-world ambiguity, multiple solutions, and implicit constraints are absent; benchmark remains highly constrained despite naturalization claims
No statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, p-values, or significance tests despite small task set (276); no error bars; Pass@K notation inconsistent across tables
Insufficient error analysis: categorizing failures into five types provides limited insight; no investigation of error cascades, fixability, or actionable remedies for persistent operational errors

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing the genuine 'Evaluation-Realism Dilemma' in GUI agent benchmarking
Novel benchmark design using knowledge-graph-based causal paths with clever linguistic decoupling via 'Hide-and-Describe' principle
Comprehensive multi-level evaluation framework (WPSR, MATCR, p-ATSR) providing fine-grained diagnostic metrics beyond simple success rates
Rigorous human verification protocol ensuring benchmark validity and deterministic ground truth
Hierarchical LightManus-Jarvis framework with strong empirical results (45.6% vs 21.1% baseline) and 75% token reduction
Extensive documentation with detailed pipeline descriptions, case studies, execution trajectories, and systematic benchmark comparison
Insightful empirical analysis revealing non-linear model performance scaling and task-dependent model capabilities
Testing across multiple model families (Gemini, GPT, Claude, Qwen) strengthens generalizability claims
Thoughtful ablation study isolating contributions of planning vs execution components
weaknesses: Dataset scale is limited (276 tasks) compared to comparable benchmarks (Mind2Web: 2,350), with imbalanced difficulty distribution (133 Level-1 vs 51 Level-3 tasks)
Acknowledged scope limitations exclude dynamic/irreversible scenarios (e-commerce, messaging), reducing real-world applicability
Framework novelty is incremental—hierarchical planning+execution is standard in AI; Context Evolution appears to be straightforward LLM-based parameter substitution

Generalization concerns: improvements on external benchmarks are much smaller (AndroidWorld: 13.6% vs 24.5% on NaturalGAIA; Mind2Web: 8.5%), suggesting optimization to benchmark rather than general GUI tasks

Critical technical details missing or unclear: Context Evolution implementation (how is Eϕ defined?), viewport semantic filter definition (what are V_vis and I_int?), positional weighting p(i) form in p-ATSR never specified
Statistical rigor insufficient: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or inter-rater reliability scores; error classification appears subjective without validation; small Level-3 sample (n=51)

Reproducibility gaps: code availability claimed but link appears redacted; missing implementation details (prompts, hyperparameters, hardware specs); no analysis of task generation computational costs
Human verification scalability bottleneck acknowledged but unaddressed; no statistics on task failure rates or discarding
Limited novelty in system design: hybrid visual-structural perception borrows from existing work; no strong theoretical contribution beyond engineering
Presentation issues: dense paper, key architectural details relegated to appendices, 'cognitive nonlinearity' vaguely defined and not formally validated
